about.whatBody: Chess is played on eight ranks and eight files by two armies of sixteen pieces. White moves first. Each piece moves its own way — the queen anywhere in a line, the knight in its L, the pawn straight ahead but capturing across — and the game ends when a king is attacked and cannot get out of it. Three moves are special: castling, where the king and a rook move together; the capture in passing, where a pawn takes another that has just stepped two squares; and promotion, where a pawn that reaches the far side becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight. A game can also end in a draw: stalemate, too little material to mate, the same position three times, or fifty moves without a capture or a pawn move.

about.engineBody: Games are analysed in your browser by Stockfish 19 (the lite, single-threaded build by Stockfish.js), used under the GPL-3.0 licence. Opening names come from the lichess opening list, which is in the public domain.
